title.zh: 卷三十六 志第十六: 天文下
title.raw: 卷三十六 志第十六: 天文下 Volume 36 Treatises 16: Astronomy 2

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

translations.literal: Treatise Twenty: Geography Three

sentences.zh: ○淮南道六江南道七隴右道八淮南道揚州，大都督府，隋江都郡。

translations.literal: ○ Huainan Circuit 6, Jiangnan Circuit 7, Longyou Circuit 8. Huainan Circuit — Yangzhou, superior-prefecture great protectorate, in Sui times the Jiangdu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Huainan Circuit 6, Jiangnan Circuit 7, Longyou Circuit 8. Huainan Circuit — Yangzhou Superior Prefecture Great Protectorate: in Sui times the Jiangdu commandery.

sentences.zh: ，杜伏威歸國，于潤州江寧縣置揚州，以隋江都郡為兗州，置東南道行臺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, when Du Fuwei submitted to the dynasty, Yangzhou was established at Jiangning County in Run Prefecture; the Sui Jiangdu commandery was made Yan Prefecture, and a Southeast Circuit mobile secretariat was set up.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3, after Du Fuwei submitted, Yangzhou was placed at Jiangning in Run Prefecture, the old Sui Jiangdu commandery became Yan Prefecture, and a southeast circuit headquarters was established.

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Yan Prefecture was changed to Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Yan Prefecture was renamed Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九年，省江寧縣之揚州，改邗州為揚州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Yangzhou at Jiangning County was abolished, and Han Prefecture was changed to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the Yangzhou seat at Jiangning was abolished and Han Prefecture was renamed Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 置大都督，督揚、和、滁、楚、舒、廬、壽七州。

translations.literal: A great protectorate was established, supervising Yang, He, Chuzhou, Chu, Shu, Lu, and Shou — seven prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: A great protectorate was installed to oversee Yang, He, Chuzhou, Chu, Shu, Lu, and Shou — seven prefectures.

sentences.zh: ，改大都督為都督，督揚、滁、常、潤、和、宣、歙七州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan, the great protectorate was changed to a protectorate, supervising Yang, Chu, Chang, Run, He, Xuan, and She — seven prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10, the great protectorate became a protectorate overseeing Yang, Chu, Chang, Run, He, Xuan, and She.

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, it was elevated to a great-protectorate prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 it was raised to a great-protectorate prefecture.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, it was changed to the Guangling commandery, while retaining the great-protectorate prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 it became the Guangling commandery, still a great-protectorate prefecture.

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, it was again made Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 it was restored as Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 自後置淮南節度使，親王為都督，領使；

translations.literal: Thereafter the Huainan military commissioner was established; an imperial prince served as protector and held the commission;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward a Huainan military commissioner was appointed; an imperial prince served as protector and held the commission;

sentences.zh: 長史為節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: the chief administrator was deputy military commissioner and handled commissioner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: the chief administrator served as deputy commissioner and managed frontier affairs.

translations.literal: This was constantly used as the seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: The seat of government was always here.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣四：江都、六合、海陵、高郵、戶二萬三千一百九十九，口九萬四千三百四十七。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed four counties — Jiangdu, Liuhe, Hailing, and Gaoyou — with 23,199 households and a population of 94,347.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly governed four counties — Jiangdu, Liuhe, Hailing, and Gaoyou — with 23,199 households and 94,347 persons.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣七，戶七萬七千一百五，口四十六萬七千八百五十七。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed seven counties, with 77,105 households and a population of 467,857.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao it governed seven counties, with 77,105 households and 467,857 persons.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南二千七百五十三里，至東都一千七百四十九里。

translations.literal: It stood 2,753 li southeast of the capital and 1,749 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 2,753 li southeast of Chang'an and 1,749 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Jiangdu: a county of Han times, subordinate to the Guangling kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdu: a Han county in Guangling kingdom.

translations.literal: Under the Sui it was the Jiangdu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui it formed the Jiangdu commandery.

sentences.zh: ，改為兗州，七年改為邗州，九年改為揚州都督府，皆以江都為治所

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude it was changed to Yan Prefecture; in the seventh year to Han Prefecture; in the ninth year to the Yangzhou protectorate prefecture — in each case with Jiangdu as the seat.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 it became Yan Prefecture; in year 7 Han Prefecture; in year 9 the Yangzhou protectorate — always seated at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: ，，分江都縣置，在郭下，與江都分理

translations.literal: Jiangyang: in the eighteenth year of Zhenguan, established by division from Jiangdu County; it lay within the outer wards and was administered separately from Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyang: created in Zhenguan 18 from Jiangdu, within the city environs and administered apart from Jiangdu.

translations.literal: Liuhe: in Han times Tangyi County, subordinate to Linhuai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe: the Han county of Tangyi in Linhuai commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉置秦郡，北齊為秦州，後周為方州，隋改為兗州。

translations.literal: The Jin established Qin Commandery; the Northern Qi made it Qin Prefecture; the Later Zhou made it Fang Prefecture; the Sui changed it to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jin set up Qin commandery; Northern Qi made it Qin prefecture; Later Zhou Fang prefecture; the Sui renamed it Yan.

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wude it was again made Fang Prefecture and Liuhe County was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 7 it became Fang Prefecture again and Liuhe County was established.

translations.literal: Shiliang County was further established by division from Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang County was then split off from Liuhe.

sentences.zh: ，省方州，並石樑入六合，屬揚州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, Fang Prefecture was abolished, Shiliang was merged into Liuhe, and it was placed under Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 Fang Prefecture was abolished, Shiliang merged into Liuhe, and the county came under Yangzhou.

translations.literal: Hailing: a Han county, subordinate to Linhuai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing: a Han county in Linhuai commandery.

translations.literal: By the Sui it belonged to Southern Gun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui it belonged to Southern Gun Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude it was placed under Yangzhou; in the second year of Jinglong, Haian County was established by division.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2 it came under Yangzhou; in Jinglong 2 Haian County was established.

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan it was abolished and merged into Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 10 it was abolished and merged into Hailing.

translations.literal: Gaoyou: a Han county, subordinate to the Guangling kingdom, unchanged through the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyou: a Han county in Guangling kingdom, unchanged under the Sui.

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude it was placed under Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2 it was assigned to Yan Prefecture.

translations.literal: When the prefecture was renamed, it remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture changed names, the county followed as before.

translations.literal: Yangzi: in the first year of Yongchun, established by division from Jiangdu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzi: established in Yongchun 1 by division from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: ，，割江都、六合、高郵三縣地置千秋縣，天寶七載，改為天長。

translations.literal: Tianchang: in the first year of Tianbao, territory was taken from Jiangdu, Liuhe, and Gaoyou to establish Qianqiu County; in the seventh year of Tianbao it was changed to Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianchang: in Tianbao 1 land from Jiangdu, Liuhe, and Gaoyou was carved out as Qianqiu County; in Tianbao 7 it was renamed Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 楚州，中，隋江都郡之山陽縣。

translations.literal: Chu Prefecture, middle grade: in Sui times Shanyang County of the Jiangdu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Prefecture, middle grade: in Sui times Shanyang County in the Jiangdu commandery.

sentences.zh: ，臧君相歸附，立為東楚州，領山陽、安且、鹽城三縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Zang Junxiang submitted, it was established as Eastern Chu Prefecture, governing Shanyang, Anqie, and Yancheng — three counties.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 4, when Zang Junxiang submitted, it became Eastern Chu Prefecture, governing Shanyang, Anqie, and Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢西楚州，以盱眙來屬，仍去「東」字。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Western Chu Prefecture was abolished, Xuyi was brought under it, and the word "Eastern" was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Western Chu was abolished, Xuyi was added, and the "Eastern" prefix was dropped.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, it was changed to the Huaiyin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 it became the Huaiyin commandery.

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, it was again made Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 it was restored as Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣四，戶三千三百五十七。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed four counties, with 3,357 households.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly governed four counties with 3,357 households.

sentences.zh: 口一萬六千二百六十二。

translations.literal: The population was 16,262.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣五，戶二萬六千六十二，口十五萬三千。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed five counties, with 26,062 households and a population of 153,000.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao it governed five counties with 26,062 households and 153,000 persons.

sentences.zh: 在京師西南二千五百一里，至東都一千六百六十里。

translations.literal: It stood 2,501 li southwest of the capital and 1,660 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 2,501 li southwest of Chang'an and 1,660 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Shanyang: the territory of Han-era Sheyang County, subordinate to Linhuai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang: Han Sheyang territory in Linhuai commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉置山陽郡，改為山陽縣。

translations.literal: The Jin established Shanyang Commandery and changed it to Shanyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Jin established Shanyang commandery, then Shanyang County.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, Eastern Chu Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 4 Eastern Chu Prefecture was established.

translations.literal: In the eighth year the word "Eastern" was dropped, and the seat was at this county.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the "Eastern" prefix was dropped and the seat lay here.

translations.literal: Southeast of the county is Sheyang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the county lies Sheyang Lake.

translations.literal: Yancheng: the territory of Han-era Yandu County, subordinate to Linhuai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yancheng: Han Yandu territory in Linhuai commandery.

sentences.zh: 久無城邑，隋末，韋徹於此置射州，立射陽、安樂、新安三縣。

translations.literal: For long there had been no walled settlement; at the end of the Sui, Wei Che established She Prefecture here and set up Sheyang, Anle, and Xin'an — three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Long without a walled town, at the end of Sui Wei Che set up She Prefecture here with Sheyang, Anle, and Xin'an.

translations.literal: When he submitted to the dynasty, the arrangement was left unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On submission the arrangement was left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 七年，廢射州及三縣，置鹽城縣於廢射州，仍屬楚州

translations.literal: In the seventh year, She Prefecture and the three counties were abolished; Yancheng County was established on the site of the abolished She Prefecture and remained under Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year She Prefecture and its three counties were abolished; Yancheng was established on the old site and remained under Chu.

translations.literal: Xuyi: a Han county, subordinate to Linhuai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi: a Han county in Linhuai commandery.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, Western Chu Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 4 Western Chu Prefecture was established.

translations.literal: A superintendent was installed to oversee Eastern and Western Chu.
translations.idiomatic: A superintendent was placed over Eastern and Western Chu.

translations.literal: It governed Xuyi alone.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢西楚州，以盱眙屬楚州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Western Chu Prefecture was abolished and Xuyi was placed under Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Western Chu was abolished and Xuyi passed to Chu.

sentences.zh: 寶應漢平安縣，屬廣陵國。

translations.literal: Anyi (later Baoying): in Han times Ping'an County, subordinate to the Guangling kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Anyi (later Baoying): the Han county of Ping'an in Guangling kingdom.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, Cang Prefecture was established, governing Anyi alone.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 4 Cang Prefecture was established, governing Anyi alone.

translations.literal: In the seventh year the prefecture was abolished and the county was placed under Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the prefecture was abolished and the county came under Chu.

sentences.zh: 肅宗建巳月，於此縣得定國寶十三枚，因改元寶應，仍改安宜為寶應

translations.literal: In the jiansi month of the third year of Shangyuan under Emperor Suzong, thirteen treasures of the realm were found in this county; the reign era was therefore changed to Baoying, and Anyi was renamed Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiansi month of Shangyuan 3, Emperor Suzong found thirteen imperial treasures here; the era was renamed Baoying and Anyi became Baoying County.

translations.literal: Huaiyin: in the second year of Qianfeng, established by division from Shanyang County on the site of a Sui-era abolished county.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyin: in Qianfeng 2 it was split from Shanyang on a former Sui county site.

sentences.zh: 滁州，下，隋江都之清流縣。

translations.literal: Chuzhou Prefecture, lower grade: in Sui times Qingliu County of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou, lower grade: in Sui times Qingliu County in Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: ，杜伏威歸國，置滁州，又以揚州之全椒來屬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, when Du Fuwei submitted, Chuzhou was established, and Quanjiao from Yang Prefecture was also brought under it.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3, after Du Fuwei submitted, Chuzhou was established and Quanjiao from Yang was added.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, it was changed to the Yongyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 it became the Yongyang commandery.

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, it was again made Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 it was restored as Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣二，戶四千六百八十九，口二萬一千五百三十五。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed two counties, with 4,689 households and a population of 21,535.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly governed two counties with 4,689 households and 21,535 persons.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣三，戶二萬六千四百八十六，口十五萬二千三百七十四。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed three counties, with 26,486 households and a population of 152,374.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao it governed three counties with 26,486 households and 152,374 persons.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南二千五百六十四里，至東都一千七百四十六里。

translations.literal: It stood 2,564 li southeast of the capital and 1,746 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 2,564 li southeast of Chang'an and 1,746 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Qingliu: the territory of Han-era Quanjiao County, subordinate to Jiujiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qingliu: Han Quanjiao territory in Jiujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 梁置南譙州，居桑根山之朝陽，在今縣西南八十里南譙州故城是也。

translations.literal: The Liang established Southern Qiao Prefecture at Chaoyang on Mount Sanggen; this is the old Southern Qiao Prefecture city eighty li southwest of the present county.
translations.idiomatic: Liang set up Southern Qiao Prefecture at Chaoyang on Mount Sanggen — the old city eighty li southwest of today's county.

sentences.zh: 北齊自南譙故城經治於此新昌郡城，今州治是也。

translations.literal: The Northern Qi moved administration from the old Southern Qiao city to the Xinchang commandery city here — the present prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi shifted the seat from old Southern Qiao to the Xinchang commandery town — today's prefectural seat.

translations.literal: The Sui changed Southern Qiao to Chu Prefecture, then later abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui renamed Southern Qiao to Chu Prefecture, then abolished it.

translations.literal: When restored, the seat was always at Qingliu County.
translations.idiomatic: On restoration the seat was always at Qingliu.

translations.literal: Quanjiao: the old Han county name.
translations.idiomatic: Quanjiao: the old Han county name.

sentences.zh: 梁北譙郡，又改為臨滁郡。

translations.literal: Under the Liang it was Northern Qiao Commandery, then changed to Linchu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang it was Northern Qiao commandery, then Linchu commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋改為滁縣，煬帝復為全椒。

translations.literal: The Sui changed it to Chu County; Emperor Yang restored the name Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui renamed it Chu County; Emperor Yang restored Quanjiao.

translations.literal: Yongyang: established by division from Qingliu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyang: established by division from Qingliu.

translations.literal: He Prefecture: in Sui times the Liyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He Prefecture: in Sui times the Liyang commandery.

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, when Du Fuwei submitted, it was changed to He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3, after Du Fuwei submitted, it became He Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, it was changed to the Liyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 it became the Liyang commandery.

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, it was again made He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 it was restored as He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣二，戶五千七百三十，口三萬三千四百一。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed two counties, with 5,730 households and a population of 33,401.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly governed two counties with 5,730 households and 33,401 persons.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣三，戶二萬四千七百九十四，口十二萬一千一十三。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed three counties, with 24,794 households and a population of 121,013.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao it governed three counties with 24,794 households and 121,013 persons.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南二千六百八十三里，至東都一千八百一十一里。

translations.literal: It stood 2,683 li southeast of the capital and 1,811 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 2,683 li southeast of Chang'an and 1,811 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Liyang: a Han county, subordinate to Jiujiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liyang: a Han county in Jiujiang commandery.

translations.literal: Eastern Jin established Liyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋為南豫州，北齊置和州。

translations.literal: Under Song it was Southern Yu Prefecture; the Northern Qi established He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Song made it Southern Yu Prefecture; Northern Qi established He Prefecture.

translations.literal: Under the Sui it was the Liyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui it was the Liyang commandery.

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, it was again made He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding it again became He Prefecture.

translations.literal: In every case the seat was at this county.
translations.idiomatic: The seat was always at this county.

sentences.zh: ，漢東城縣之烏江亭，屬九江郡。

translations.literal: Wujiang: the Wujiang pavilion of Han-era Dongcheng County, subordinate to Jiujiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wujiang: the Wujiang pavilion of Han Dongcheng in Jiujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 北齊為密江郡，陳為臨江郡，後周為問江郡，隋為烏江郡，縣皆治此

translations.literal: The Northern Qi made it Mijiang Commandery; Chen made it Linjiang Commandery; the Later Zhou made it Wenjiang Commandery; the Sui made it Wujiang Commandery — in each case the county seat was here.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi made it Mijiang commandery; Chen Linjiang; Later Zhou Wenjiang; Sui Wujiang — the seat was always here.

translations.literal: Hanshan: established in the sixth year of Wude; abolished in the eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Hanshan: established in Wude 6; abolished in Wude 8.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chang'an it was restored as Wushou County.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 4 it was restored as Wushou County.

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong it was again made Hanshan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 1 it was again named Hanshan.

translations.literal: Hao Prefecture, lower grade: in Sui times the Zhongli commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Prefecture, lower grade: in Sui times the Zhongli commandery.

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, it was changed to Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 it became Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又改臨濠為定遠縣，化明為招義縣。

translations.literal: Linhao was further changed to Dingyuan County and Huaming to Zhaoyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Linhao was renamed Dingyuan and Huaming Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 領鐘離、塗山、定遠、招義四縣。

translations.literal: It governed Zhongli, Tushan, Dingyuan, and Zhaoyi — four counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed Zhongli, Tushan, Dingyuan, and Zhaoyi.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, Tushan was abolished and merged into Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 4, Tushan was abolished and merged into Zhongli.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, it was changed to the Zhongli commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 it became the Zhongli commandery.

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, it was again made Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 it was restored as Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣三，戶二千六百六十，口一萬三千八百五十五。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed three counties, with 2,660 households and 13,855 mouths.
translations.idiomatic: It formerly governed three counties, with 2,660 households and 13,855 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶二萬一千八百六十四，口十萬八千三百六十一。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao, there were 21,864 households and 108,361 mouths.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era it had 21,864 households and 108,361 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南二千一百五十里，至東都一千三百一十三里。

translations.literal: It lay 2,150 li southeast of the capital and 1,313 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It was 2,150 li southeast of the capital and 1,313 li from the Eastern Capital.

translations.literal: Zhongli, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Jiujiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli was a Han county under the Jiujiang commandery.

translations.literal: Under Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang, Xuzhou was established here.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang, Xuzhou was placed here.

sentences.zh: 隋初為濠州，煬帝復為鐘離郡。

translations.literal: In early Sui it was Hao Prefecture; under Emperor Yang it again became the Zhongli commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In early Sui it was Hao Prefecture; under Emperor Yang it became the Zhongli commandery again.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南二千八百二十一里，至東都一千七百九十七里。

After the Zhide era it was again made Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣三，戶四千六百八十，口一萬三千七百二。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed three counties, with 4,680 households and 13,702 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南六千一百七十三里，至東都五千三百七十里。

translations.literal: It lay 6,173 li southeast of the capital and 5,370 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 6,173 li southeast of the capital, 5,370 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Changting was the seat of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 龍岩寧化已上三縣，並開山洞置。

translations.literal: Longyan, Ninghua — the three counties above were all established by opening mountain caves.
translations.idiomatic: Longyan and Ninghua — all three by opening caves.

translations.literal: Zhang Prefecture was established on the ninth day of the twelfth month of the second year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 2, twelfth month, day 9: Zhang established.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Zhangpu commandery.

sentences.zh: 舊屬嶺南道，天寶割屬江南東道。

translations.literal: Formerly subordinate to Lingnan Circuit; in Tianbao it was detached to Eastern Jiangnan Circuit.
After the Zhide era it was again made Zhang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣二，戶五千三百四十六，口一萬七千九百四十。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed two counties, with 5,346 households and 17,940 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南七千三百里，至東都六千五百里。

translations.literal: It lay 7,300 li southeast of the capital and 6,500 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 7,300 li southeast of the capital, 6,500 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month it was established together with the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: established with the prefecture.

translations.literal: Zhangpu was the seat of the prefecture.
Formerly subordinate to Quan Prefecture.
In the fourth year of Zhenguan it was subordinate to Wurong Prefecture.
It returned to Quan Prefecture.
In the second year of Tianbao it was subordinate to Zhang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 江南西道宣州隋宣城郡。

translations.literal: Xuan Prefecture of Western Jiangnan Circuit, in Sui times the Xuancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Prefecture, Western Jiangnan: Sui Xuancheng commandery.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Du Fuwei submitted,
the Xuanzhou protectorate was established.

sentences.zh: 分宣城置懷安、甯國二縣。

translations.literal: Huai'an and Ningguo — two counties — were split off from Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'an and Ningguo split from Xuancheng.

translations.literal: In the sixth year it fell to Fu Gongshi.

sentences.zh: 七年賊平，改置宣州都督，督宣、潛、猷、池四州，廢桃州，以綏安來屬，省懷安、甯國二縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the rebels were pacified; Xuan was made a protectorate-general supervising Xuan, Qian, You, and Chi — four prefectures; Tao Prefecture was abolished and Suian assigned here; Huai'an and Ningguo — two counties — were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 7: rebels pacified; Xuan protectorate-general over four prefectures; Tao abolished; Suian here; Huai'an and Ningguo abolished.

translations.literal: Xuan Prefecture governed Xuancheng and Suian — two counties.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢南豫州，以當塗來屬，廢猷州，以涇縣來屬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Southern Yu Prefecture was abolished and Dangtu assigned here; You Prefecture was abolished and Jing County assigned here.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Southern Yu abolished, Dangtu here; You abolished, Jing here.

sentences.zh: 九年，移揚州于江都，以溧陽、溧水、丹陽來屬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Yang Prefecture moved to Jiangdu; Liyang, Lishui, and Danyang were assigned here.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 9: Yang to Jiangdu; Liyang, Lishui, Danyang here.

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan the protectorate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 廢池州，以秋浦、南陵二縣來屬。

translations.literal: Chi Prefecture was abolished and Qiupu and Nanling — two counties — were assigned here.
translations.idiomatic: Chi abolished; Qiupu and Nanling here.

translations.literal: Danyang was abolished and merged into Dangtu County.

sentences.zh: 開元中，析置青陽、太平、甯國三縣，，改為宣城郡。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era Qingyang, Taiping, and Ningguo — three counties — were split off and it was changed to the Xuancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan: Qingyang, Taiping, Ningguo split; Xuancheng commandery.

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao Zhide County was also split off.
After the Zhide era it was again made Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: ，割秋浦、青陽、至德三縣置池州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao Qiupu, Qingyang, and Zhide — three counties — were detached to establish Chi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 3: Qiupu, Qingyang, Zhide to Chi.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣八，戶二萬二千五百三十七，口九萬五千七百五十三。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed eight counties, with 22,537 households and 95,753 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣九，戶一十二萬一千二百四，口八十八萬四千九百八十五。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed nine counties, with 121,204 households and 884,985 mouths.
At present there are ten counties.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南三千五百五十一里，至東都二千五百一十里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,551 li southeast of the capital and 2,510 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,551 li southeast of the capital, 2,510 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Xuancheng, Han Wanling County, subordinate to Danyang commandery.
Under the Qin it was part of Zhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 梁置南豫州，隋改為宣州，煬帝又為宣城郡，皆此治所

translations.literal: The Liang established Southern Yu Prefecture; the Sui changed it to Xuan Prefecture; Emperor Yang again made the Xuancheng commandery; all were at this seat.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Southern Yu; Sui Xuan; Yang Xuancheng commandery; all at this seat.

translations.literal: Dangtu, the territory of Han Danyang County, subordinate to Danyang commandery.
The Jin split Danyang to establish Yuhu County.

sentences.zh: 成帝以江北當塗縣流人寓居於湖，乃改為當塗縣，屬宣州。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng made displaced people from Dangtu north of the river reside at Yuhu and therefore changed it to Dangtu County, subordinate to Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng: north-of-river Dangtu migrants at Yuhu; Dangtu County, Xuan.

sentences.zh: 牛渚山，一名採石，在縣北四十五里大江中。

translations.literal: Niuzhu Mountain, also called Caishi, lies in the great river forty-five li north of the county.
translations.idiomatic: Niuzhu, also Caishi, 45 li north in the great river.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude Southern Yu Prefecture was established and the county was assigned to it.

sentences.zh: 八年，省南豫州，縣屬宣州

translations.literal: In the eighth year Southern Yu Prefecture was abolished and the county was assigned to Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Southern Yu abolished; county to Xuan.

translations.literal: Jing, Han Jing County, subordinate to Danyang commandery.
In the fourth year of Wude You Prefecture was established, governing Jing, Nanyang, and Anwu — three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: You with Jing, Nanyang, Anwu.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢猷州及南陽、安吳二縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year You Prefecture and Nanyang and Anwu — two counties — were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: You abolished; Nanyang and Anwu abolished.

translations.literal: It was subordinate to Xuan Prefecture.
Within the county bounds is Lingyang Mountain.
Guangde, Han Guzhang County, subordinate to Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋分宣城之廣德、吳興之故鄣，置綏安縣。

translations.literal: The Song split Guangde of Xuancheng and Guzhang of Wuxing to establish Suian County.
translations.idiomatic: Song: Guangde of Xuancheng and Wuxing Guzhang; Suian.

sentences.zh: 九月，改為廣德，以縣界廣德故城為名

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Tianbao it was changed to Guangde, taking the name from the old Guangde city within the county bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 2, ninth month: Guangde, from old city in bounds.

translations.literal: Lishui, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Danyang commandery.
In the eleventh month of the second year of Tianbao it was detached to Sheng Prefecture.
When the prefecture was abolished it was assigned here.
Liyang, Han Liyang territory.
Under the Sui it was a county.
In the fourth year of Wude it was subordinate to Yang Prefecture.
In the ninth year it was subordinate to Xuan Prefecture.
It was subordinate to Sheng Prefecture.
When the prefecture was abolished it returned here.
Nanling, the territory of Han Chungu County, subordinate to Danyang commandery.
The Liang established Nanling County.
In the fourth year of Wude it was subordinate to Chi Prefecture.
When the prefectorate was abolished it was assigned here.

sentences.zh: 舊治赭圻城，，移理青陽城

translations.literal: Formerly administered at Zheqi walled city; in the third year of Tianbao the seat was moved to Qingyang walled city.
translations.idiomatic: Former seat Zheqi; Tianbao 3 moved to Qingyang.

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Tianbao it was split off from Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 3, first month: split from Jing.

translations.literal: Taiping, a Sui dynasty county.
Abolished; restored.
In the second month of the second year of Tianbao it was split off from Taiping County.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 2, second month: split from Taiping.

sentences.zh: 池州下，隋宣城郡之秋浦縣。

translations.literal: Chi Prefecture, lower grade, in Sui times Qiupu County of the Xuancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Prefecture, lower grade: Sui Qiupu in Xuancheng commandery.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude Chi Prefecture was established, governing Qiupu and Nanling — two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Chi with Qiupu and Nanling.

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan Chi Prefecture was abolished and Qiupu was assigned to Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 1: Chi abolished; Qiupu to Xuan.

sentences.zh: ，江西觀察使李勉以秋浦去洪州九百里，請復置池州，仍請割青陽、至德二縣隸之，又析置石埭縣，並從之。

translations.literal: Later the Jiangxi observation commissioner Li Mian, because Qiupu was nine hundred li from Hong Prefecture, requested that Chi Prefecture be re-established; he also requested that Qingyang and Zhide — two counties — be subordinated to it and Shiling County be split off; all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian: Qiupu 900 li from Hong; Chi restored; Qingyang and Zhide subordinated; Shiling split; granted.

translations.literal: Later it was subordinate to Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 領縣四，戶一萬九千，口八萬七千九百六十七。

translations.literal: It governed four counties, with 19,000 households and 87,967 mouths.
Qiupu was the seat of the prefecture.
Qiupu, Han Shicheng County, subordinate to Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋分南陵置秋浦縣，因水為名

translations.literal: The Sui split Nanling to establish Qiupu County, named for the river.
translations.idiomatic: Sui split Nanling for Qiupu, named for the river.

sentences.zh: ，分涇、南陵、秋浦三縣置，治古臨城

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was established by splitting Jing, Nanling, and Qiupu — three counties — administered from ancient Lincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 1: from Jing, Nanling, Qiupu; seat at ancient Lincheng.

translations.literal: Split off and established.

sentences.zh: ，割秋浦、浮梁、黟三縣置，治古石埭城。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao it was established by detaching Qiupu, Fuliang, and Yi — three counties — administered from the ancient Shiling walled city.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 3: from Qiupu, Fuliang, Yi; ancient Shiling city.

translations.literal: Rao Prefecture, lower grade, in Sui times the Poyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rao Prefecture, lower grade: Sui Poyang commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平江左，置饒州，領鄱陽、新平、廣晉、餘幹、樂平、長城、玉亭、弋陽、上饒九縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when the Jiangzuo region was pacified, Rao Prefecture was established, governing Poyang, Xinping, Guangjin, Yugan, Leping, Changcheng, Yuting, Yiyang, and Shangrao — nine counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Jiangzuo pacified; Rao with nine counties.

sentences.zh: 七年，省上饒入弋陽，省玉亭入長城、餘幹二縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Shangrao was abolished and merged into Yiyang; Yuting was abolished and merged into Changcheng and Yugan — two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 7: Shangrao into Yiyang; Yuting into Changcheng and Yugan.

sentences.zh: 八年，又並長城入餘幹，並新平、廣晉入鄱陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Changcheng was again merged into Yugan; Xinping and Guangjin were merged into Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Changcheng into Yugan; Xinping and Guangjin into Poyang.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣四，戶一萬一千四百，口五萬九千八百一十七。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed four counties, with 11,400 households and 59,817 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶四萬八百九十九，口二十四萬四千三百五十。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao there were 40,899 households and 244,350 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南三千二百六十三里，至東都二千四百一十三里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,263 li southeast of the capital and 2,413 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,263 li southeast of the capital, 2,413 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Poyang, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 古城在今縣東界，有鄱江，今為州所理

translations.literal: The old city lies on the eastern border of the present county; there is the Po River; it is now the seat of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Old city on east border; Po River; now prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Yugan, Han Yugan County, subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.
It was what the ancients called the Gan Yue.
Gan is pronounced gan; the Sui dropped the water radical.
translations.idiomatic: Gan pronounced gan; Sui dropped water radical.

sentences.zh: 樂平武德中置，九年省，後重置

translations.literal: Leping was established in the Wude era; abolished in the ninth year and later re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Wude: Leping; Wude 9 abolished; later restored.

translations.literal: In the Wude era Xinping County was abolished.
In the fourth year of Wude it was split off from Poyang and established; later changed to Xinchang.
Re-established.

sentences.zh: 洪州上，都督府，隋豫章郡。

translations.literal: Hong Prefecture, upper grade, protectorate, in Sui times the Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Prefecture, upper grade, protectorate: Sui Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平林士弘，置洪州總管府，管洪、饒、撫、吉、虔、南平六州，分豫章置鐘陵縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Lin Shihong was pacified, the Hongzhou protectorate was established supervising Hong, Rao, Fu, Ji, Qian, and Nanping — six prefectures; Zhongling County was split off from Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Lin Shihong pacified; Hong protectorate over six prefectures; Zhongling from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 洪州領豫章、豐城、鐘陵三縣。

translations.literal: Hong Prefecture governed Yuzhang, Fengcheng, and Zhongling — three counties.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢孫州、南昌州、米州，以南昌、建昌、高安三縣來屬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Sun, Nanchang, and Mi — three prefectures — were abolished; Nanchang, Jianchang, and Gao'an — three counties — were assigned here.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Sun, Nanchang, Mi abolished; three counties here.

sentences.zh: 省鐘陵、南昌二縣入豫章。

translations.literal: Zhongling and Nanchang — two counties — were abolished and merged into Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: ，加洪、饒、撫、吉、虔、袁、江、鄂等八州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan Hong, Rao, Fu, Ji, Qian, Yuan, Jiang, and E — eight prefectures — were added.
It supervised Rao, E, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 洪州舊領縣四，，置新吳縣。

translations.literal: Hong Prefecture formerly governed four counties; in the second year of Tianbao Xinwu County was established.

sentences.zh: ，置武寧縣，又督洪、袁、吉、虔、撫五州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao Wuning County was established; it also supervised Hong, Yuan, Ji, Qian, and Fu — five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 2: Wuning; also supervised five prefectures.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Yuzhang commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣四：豫章、豐城、高安、建昌。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed four counties: Yuzhang, Fengcheng, Gao'an, and Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 戶一萬五千四百五十六，口七萬四千四十四。

translations.literal: There were 15,456 households and 74,044 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣六，戶五萬五千五百三十，口三十五萬三千二百三十一。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed six counties, with 55,530 households and 353,231 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南三千九十里，至東都二千二百一十一里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,090 li southeast of the capital and 2,211 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,090 li southeast of the capital, 2,211 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 漢南昌縣，豫章郡所治也。

translations.literal: Yuzhang, Han Nanchang County, was the seat of Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhang: Han Nanchang, Yuzhang commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 隋改為豫章縣，置洪州，煬帝復為豫章郡。

translations.literal: The Sui changed it to Yuzhang County and established Hong Prefecture; Emperor Yang again made the Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Yuzhang County and Hong; Yang Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 六月，以犯代宗諱，改為鐘陵，取地名

translations.literal: In the sixth month it was changed to Zhongling to avoid the taboo of Emperor Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: Zhongling, avoiding Daizong taboo.

sentences.zh: 吳分南昌縣置富城縣，晉改為豐城

translations.literal: Wu split Nanchang to establish Fucheng County; the Jin changed it to Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Nanchang for Fucheng; Jin Fengcheng.

translations.literal: Gao'an, Han Jiancheng County, subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: ，改為高安，仍置靖州，領高安、望蔡、華陽三縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude it was changed to Gao'an and Jing Prefecture was still established, governing Gao'an, Wangcai, and Huayang — three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Gao'an; Jing with three counties.

translations.literal: In the seventh year Jing Prefecture was changed to Mi Prefecture.
That same year it was again changed to Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢筠州，省華陽、望蔡二縣，以高安屬洪州

translations.literal: In the eighth year Yun Prefecture was abolished; Huayang and Wangcai — two counties — were abolished and Gao'an was assigned to Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Yun abolished; two counties abolished; Gao'an to Hong.

translations.literal: Jianchang, Han Haihun County, subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.
Later Han split off and established Jianchang.

sentences.zh: ，分置南昌州總管府，管南昌、西吳、靖、米、孫五州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude the Nanchangzhou protectorate was split off and established, supervising Nanchang, Xiwu, Jing, Mi, and Sun — five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Nanchangzhou protectorate over five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 南昌州領建昌、龍安、永修三縣。

translations.literal: Nanchangzhou governed Jianchang, Long'an, and Yongxiu — three counties.
In the seventh year the protectorate was abolished to become Nanchang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢南昌州及孫州，以南昌州新吳、永修、龍安入建昌縣，以孫州之建昌入豫章縣，而以建昌屬洪州

translations.literal: In the eighth year Nanchang Prefecture and Sun Prefecture were abolished; Xinwu, Yongxiu, and Long'an of Nanchangzhou were merged into Jianchang County; Jianchang of Sun Prefecture was merged into Yuzhang County; and Jianchang was assigned to Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Nanchang and Sun abolished; mergers; Jianchang to Hong.

translations.literal: A long-abolished county.
In the second year of Tianbao it was split off from Jianchang and established.
In the second year of Tianbao Wuning County was split off from Jianchang.
In the first year of Qianyuan it was changed to Yuning.
In the first year of Zhenyuan it was again made Wuning.
Established in the second month.
Qian Prefecture, middle grade, in Sui times the Nankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Prefecture, middle grade: Sui Nankang commandery.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when the Jiangzuo region was pacified, Qian Prefecture was established.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Nankang commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣四，戶八千九百九十四，口三萬九千九百一。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed four counties, with 8,994 households and 39,901 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣六，戶三萬七千六百四十七，口二十七萬五千四百一十。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed six counties, with 37,647 households and 275,410 mouths.
At present there are seven counties.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南四千一十七里，至東都三千四百里。

translations.literal: It lay 4,017 li southeast of the capital and 3,400 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 4,017 li southeast of the capital, 3,400 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Gan County was the seat of the prefecture, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gan: prefectural seat; Han county, Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 漢分豫章立廬陵郡，晉改為南康郡。

translations.literal: Han split Yuzhang to establish the Luling commandery; the Jin changed it to the Nankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Han split Yuzhang for Luling; Jin Nankang commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋初為虔州，煬帝為南康郡。

translations.literal: In early Sui it was Qian Prefecture; under Emperor Yang it was the Nankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early Sui Qian; Yang Nankang commandery.

translations.literal: All were administered from Gan.

sentences.zh: 吳分贛立陽都縣，晉改為寧都。

translations.literal: Wu split Gan to establish Yangdu County; the Jin changed it to Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Gan for Yangdu; Jin Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，改為虔化，屬虔州

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen it was changed to Qianhua and was subordinate to Qian Prefecture.
Nankang, Han Nan County, subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 吳分南埜立南安縣，晉改為南康

translations.literal: Wu split Nanye to establish Nan'an County; the Jin changed it to Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Nanye for Nan'an; Jin Nankang.

translations.literal: Dayu, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.
In the fourth year of Wude Nan'an County was split off from Nankang.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to Xinfeng.
In the second year of Tianbao it was split off from Nankang.
Established on the fourth day of the eighth month.
Fu Prefecture, middle grade, in Sui times the Linchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Prefecture, middle grade: Sui Linchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: ，討平林士弘，置撫州，領臨川、南城、郡武、宜黃、崇仁、永城、東興、將樂八縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Lin Shihong was suppressed, Fu Prefecture was established, governing Linchuan, Nancheng, Junwu, Yihuang, Chongren, Yongcheng, Dongxing, and Jiangle — eight counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Lin Shihong suppressed; Fu with eight counties.

sentences.zh: 七年，省東興、永城、將樂三縣，以邵武隸建州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Dongxing, Yongcheng, and Jiangle — three counties — were abolished and Shaowu was assigned to Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 7: three counties abolished; Shaowu to Jian.

translations.literal: In the eighth year Yihuang County was abolished.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Linchuan commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣三，戶七千三百五十四，口四萬六百八十五。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed three counties, with 7,354 households and 40,685 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣四，戶三萬六百五，口十七萬六千三百九十四。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed four counties, with 30,605 households and 176,394 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南三千三百一十二里，至東都二千五百四十里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,312 li southeast of the capital and 2,540 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,312 li southeast of the capital, 2,540 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Linchuan was the seat of the prefecture.
Linchuan, the territory of Han Nanchang County.
Later Han split Nanchang to establish Linru County.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han split Nanchang for Linru.

sentences.zh: 吳置臨川郡，曆南朝不改。

translations.literal: Wu established the Linchuan commandery; through the Southern dynasties it was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Linchuan commandery; Southern dynasties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，改臨川郡為撫州，仍改臨汝縣為臨川縣。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen it changed the Linchuan commandery to Fu Prefecture and also changed Linru County to Linchuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Linchuan commandery to Fu; Linru to Linchuan.

translations.literal: The prefecture and commandery seats were all at this county.
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture and commandery seats at this county.

translations.literal: Nancheng, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.
In the fourth year of Wude it was split off from Nancheng and established.
Wu split Linru to establish Xinjian County.

sentences.zh: 梁改為巴山縣，仍僑置巴山郡。

translations.literal: The Liang changed it to Bashan County and also established the Bashan commandery as a refugee seat.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Bashan County; refugee Bashan commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，改巴山為崇仁縣

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen it changed Bashan to Chongren County.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Bashan to Chongren.

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao it was split off from Nancheng.
Ji Prefecture, upper grade, in Sui times the Luling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Prefecture, upper grade: Sui Luling commandery.

sentences.zh: ，討平林士弘，置吉州，領廬陵、新淦二縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Lin Shihong was suppressed, Ji Prefecture was established, governing Luling and Xingan — two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Lin Shihong suppressed; Ji with Luling and Xingan.

sentences.zh: 七年，廢潁州，以安福縣來屬。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Ying Prefecture was abolished and Anfu County was assigned here.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢南平州，乙太和縣來屬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Nanping Prefecture was abolished and Yihe County was assigned here.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Luling commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣四，戶一萬五千四十，口五萬三千二百八十五。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed four counties, with 15,040 households and 53,285 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣五，戶三萬七千七百五十二，口二十三萬七千三十二。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed five counties, with 37,752 households and 237,032 mouths.
Luling, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.
Under Later Han it was changed to Xichang.
The Sui restored it as Luling; it was the seat of the prefecture.
Formerly administered at Ziyang walled city; in the fourth year of Wude it was moved to the present site.
translations.idiomatic: Former seat Ziyang; Wude 4 moved to present site.

translations.literal: A Sui dynasty county.

sentences.zh: ，置南平州，領太和、永新、廣興、東昌四縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude Nanping Prefecture was established, governing Taihe, Yongxin, Guangxing, and Dongchang — four counties.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢南平州，以永新等三縣並太和，屬吉州

translations.literal: In the eighth year Nanping Prefecture was abolished; Yongxin and the other three counties were merged with Taihe and assigned to Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Nanping abolished; three counties with Taihe to Ji.

translations.literal: Wu established the Ancheng commandery here.

sentences.zh: 隋廢為安復，後改為安福

translations.literal: The Sui abolished it to Anfu and later changed it to Anfu.
Xingan, an old Han county subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.
Gan is pronounced gan; it is also pronounced gan.
The county was abolished.
In the second year of Tianbao it was split off from Taihe.
Jiang Prefecture, middle grade, in Sui times the Jiujiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Prefecture, middle grade: Sui Jiujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平林士弘，置江州，領湓城、潯陽、彭澤三縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Lin Shihong was pacified, Jiang Prefecture was established, governing Tuncheng, Xunyang, and Pengze — three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Lin Shihong pacified; Jiang with three counties.

sentences.zh: 五年，置總管，管江、鄂、智、浩四州，並管昌、洪四總管府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year a protectorate was established supervising Jiang, E, Zhi, and Hao — four prefectures, also supervising the Chang and Hong protectorate offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 5: protectorate over four prefectures and two protectorate offices.

sentences.zh: 又分湓城置楚城縣，分彭澤置都昌縣。

translations.literal: Chucheng County was split off from Tuncheng and Duchang County was split off from Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: Chucheng from Tuncheng; Duchang from Pengze.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢浩州及樂城縣入彭澤縣，又廢湓城入潯陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Hao Prefecture and Lecheng County were merged into Pengze County and Tuncheng was abolished and merged into Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Hao abolished; Lecheng into Pengze; Tuncheng into Xunyang.

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan the protectorate was abolished.
In the eighth year of Zhenguan Chucheng County was abolished and merged into Xunyang.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Xunyang commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣三，戶六千三百六十，口二萬五千五百九十九。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed three counties, with 6,360 households and 25,599 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶二萬九千二十五，口十五萬五千七百四十四。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao there were 29,025 households and 155,744 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南二千九百四十八里，至東都二千一百九十七里。

translations.literal: It lay 2,948 li southeast of the capital and 2,197 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 2,948 li southeast of the capital, 2,197 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Xunyang was the seat of the prefecture.
Xunyang, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Lujiang commandery.
Under the Jin Jiang Prefecture was established.

sentences.zh: 隋改為彭蠡縣，取州東南五十二里有彭蠡湖為名。

translations.literal: The Sui changed it to Pengli County, named for Lake Pengli fifty-two li southeast of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Pengli County, from Lake Pengli 52 li southeast.

sentences.zh: 煬帝改為湓城，取縣界湓水為名。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang changed it to Tuncheng, named for the Tun River within the county bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tuncheng, from Tun River in bounds.

sentences.zh: ，復為潯陽，潯水至此入江為名

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude it was again made Xunyang, named because the Xun River enters the Yangtze here.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xunyang again; Xun River enters Yangtze here.

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude it was split off from Pengze and was subordinate to Hao Prefecture.
In the eighth year Hao Prefecture was abolished and the county was assigned to Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Hao abolished; county to Jiang.

translations.literal: Pengze, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.
Under the Sui it was Longcheng County.

sentences.zh: ，置浩州，又分置都昌、樂城二縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude Hao Prefecture was established and Duchang and Lecheng — two counties — were also split off.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 5: Hao; Duchang and Lecheng split.

sentences.zh: 八年，罷浩州，以彭澤屬江州，仍省樂城入彭澤。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Hao Prefecture was abolished; Pengze was assigned to Jiang Prefecture and Lecheng was abolished and merged into Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Hao abolished; Pengze to Jiang; Lecheng into Pengze.

translations.literal: In the ninth month the censor Song Ruosi memorialized to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: censor Song Ruosi memorialized; established.

translations.literal: Yuan Prefecture, lower grade, in Sui times the Yichun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Prefecture, lower grade: Sui Yichun commandery.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Yuan Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Yuan established.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Yichun commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣三，戶四千六百三十六，口二萬五千七百一十六。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed three counties, with 4,636 households and 25,716 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶二萬七千九十一，口一十四萬四千九十六。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao there were 27,091 households and 144,096 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南三千五百八十里，至東都二千一百六十一里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,580 li southeast of the capital and 2,161 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,580 li southeast of the capital, 2,161 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Yichun was the seat of the prefecture.
Yichun, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Yuzhang commandery.
Wu made it the Ancheng commandery; the Southern dynasties left it unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ancheng commandery; Southern dynasties unchanged.

translations.literal: Under the Jin it was changed to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 隋置袁州，煬帝為宜春郡。

translations.literal: The Sui established Yuan Prefecture; under Emperor Yang it was the Yichun commandery.
It was again changed to Yichun.
Yichun is the name of a spring west of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yichun spring west of the prefecture.

translations.literal: Wine is made from this water and sent as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wine from this water sent as tribute.

sentences.zh: 吳分宜春置萍鄉縣，屬安成郡。

translations.literal: Wu split Yichun to establish Pingxiang County, subordinate to the Ancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Yichun for Pingxiang, Ancheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 吳分宜春置新喻，屬安成郡。

translations.literal: Wu split Yichun to establish Xinyu, subordinate to the Ancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Yichun for Xinyu, Ancheng commandery.

translations.literal: E Prefecture, upper grade, in Sui times the Jiangxia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: E Prefecture, upper grade: Sui Jiangxia commandery.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, it was changed to E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; E Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Jiangxia commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永泰後，置鄂嶽觀察使，領鄂、嶽、蘄、黃四州，恆以鄂州為使理所。

translations.literal: After the Yongtai era the E-Yue observation commissioner was established, governing E, Yue, Qi, and Huang — four prefectures; E Prefecture regularly served as the seat.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongtai: E-Yue commissioner over E, Yue, Qi, Huang; seat at E.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣四，戶三千七百五十四，口一萬四千六百一十五。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed four counties, with 3,754 households and 14,615 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣五，戶一萬九千一百九十，口八萬四千五百六十三。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed five counties, with 19,190 households and 84,563 mouths.

sentences.zh: 後並沔州入鄂州，以漢陽、𣿭川來屬。

translations.literal: Later Mian Prefecture was merged into E Prefecture and Hanyang and Mianchuan were assigned here.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mian merged into E; Hanyang and Mianchuan here.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南二千三百四十六里，至東都一千五百三十里。

translations.literal: It lay 2,346 li southeast of the capital and 1,530 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 2,346 li southeast of the capital, 1,530 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Jiangxia, the name of a Han commandery.

sentences.zh: 本漢沙羨縣地，屬江夏郡。

translations.literal: Originally the territory of Han Shaxian County, subordinate to Jiangxia commandery.
Under the Jin Shaxian was changed to Shayang.

sentences.zh: 江、漢二水會於州西，春秋謂之夏汭，晉、宋謂之夏口。

translations.literal: The Jiang and Han rivers meet west of the prefecture; in Spring and Autumn times it was called Xiarui; under Jin and Song it was called Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Han meet west; Spring and Autumn Xiarui; Jin and Song Xiakou.

translations.literal: The Song established the Jiangxia commandery.
Administered here.
The Sui left it unchanged.
In the fourth year of Wude it was changed to E Prefecture, taking the name of the Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: E Prefecture, from Han county name.

translations.literal: E County territory, subordinate to Jiangxia commandery.

sentences.zh: 吳分鄂置新陽縣，隋改為永興

translations.literal: Wu split E to establish Xinyang County; the Sui changed it to Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split E for Xinyang; Sui Yongxing.

translations.literal: E County of the Han, subordinate to Jiangxia commandery.

sentences.zh: 吳、晉為重鎮，以名將為鎮守

translations.literal: Under Wu and Jin it was a major stronghold; famous generals served as garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Jin major stronghold; famous generals as garrison commanders.

translations.literal: Wu split Shaxian County to establish it.
In the second year of Tianbao mountain caves were opened and it was established.
Hanyang, the territory of Han Anlu County, subordinate to Jiangxia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyang: Han Anlu territory, Jiangxia commandery.

translations.literal: Under the Jin Zhunyang County was established.

sentences.zh: 隋初為漢津縣，煬帝改為漢陽。

translations.literal: In early Sui it was Hanjin County; under Emperor Yang it was changed to Hanyang.

sentences.zh: ，平硃粲，分沔陽郡置沔州，治漢陽縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Zhu Can was pacified, Mian Prefecture was established by splitting Mianyang commandery, administered from Hanyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Zhu Can pacified; Mian from Mianyang commandery at Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀，戶一千五百一十七，口六千九百五十九。

translations.literal: Under Zhenguan there were 1,517 households and 6,959 mouths.

sentences.zh: 至，鄂岳節度使牛僧孺奏，沔州與鄂州隔江，都管一縣，請併入鄂州，從之。

translations.literal: By the Yongtai era the E-Yue military commissioner Niu Sengru memorialized that Mian Prefecture was separated from E Prefecture by the river and governed only one county; he requested merger into E Prefecture and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtai: Niu Sengru; Mian across river from E, one county; merged into E; granted.

translations.literal: Formerly subordinate to Huainan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 漢安陸縣地，後魏置𣿭川郡。

translations.literal: Mianchuan, the territory of Han Anlu County; Northern Wei established the Mianchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mianchuan: Han Anlu; Northern Wei Mianchuan commandery.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude Mianchuan County was split off from Hanyang County and was subordinate to Mian Prefecture.
When the prefecture was abolished it was assigned to E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian abolished, assigned to E.

translations.literal: Yue Prefecture, lower grade, in Sui times the Baling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Prefecture, lower grade: Sui Baling commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平蕭銑，置巴州，領巴陵、華容、沅江、羅、湘陰五縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Ba Prefecture was established, governing Baling, Huarong, Yuanjiang, Luo, and Xiangyin — five counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Ba with five counties.

translations.literal: In the sixth year it was changed to Yue Prefecture.
Luo County was abolished.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Baling commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣四，戶四千二，口一萬七千五百五十六。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed four counties, with 4,002 households and 17,556 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣五，戶一萬一千七百四十，口五萬二百九十八。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed five counties, with 11,740 households and 50,298 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南二千二百三十七里，至東都一千八百一十六里。

translations.literal: It lay 2,237 li southeast of the capital and 1,816 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 2,237 li southeast of the capital, 1,816 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Baling, Han Xiajun County, subordinate to Changsha commandery.
Wu established Baling County.

sentences.zh: 晉置建昌郡，隋改為巴州，煬帝改為巴陵郡。

translations.literal: Under the Jin the Jianchang commandery was established; the Sui changed it to Ba Prefecture and Emperor Yang to the Baling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Jianchang commandery; Sui Ba Prefecture; Yang Baling commandery.

sentences.zh: 武德置岳州，皆置巴陵縣。

translations.literal: In the Wude era Yue Prefecture was established; Baling County was always established.
translations.idiomatic: Wude: Yue established; Baling always established.

translations.literal: Within the county bounds is the ancient Baqiu.

sentences.zh: 漢孱陵縣地，屬武陵郡，劉表改為安南。

translations.literal: Huarong, the territory of Han Canling County, subordinate to Wuling commandery; Liu Biao changed it to Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Huarong: Han Canling, Wuling; Liu Biao Annan.

translations.literal: The Sui changed it to Huarong.
In the first year of Qianyuan the character hua was dropped and it was called Rongcheng.
In the second year of Baoying it was again made Huarong.
Yuanjiang, Han Yiyang County, subordinate to the Changsha kingdom.

sentences.zh: 隋改為安樂，又改為沅江，屬岳州

translations.literal: The Sui changed it to Anle and then to Yuanjiang, subordinate to Yue Prefecture.
Luo, Han Luo County, subordinate to the Changsha kingdom.

sentences.zh: 宋置湘陰縣，縣界汨水，注入湘江

translations.literal: The Song established Xiangyin County; within the bounds the Mi River flows into the Xiang River.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xiangyin; Mi River into Xiang within bounds.

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao it was split off from Xiangyin County.

sentences.zh: 潭州中，都督府，隋長沙郡。

translations.literal: Tan Prefecture, middle grade, protectorate, in Sui times the Changsha commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Prefecture, middle protectorate: Sui Changsha commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平蕭銑，置潭州總管府，管潭、衡、永、郴、連、南梁、南雲、南營八州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, the Tanzhou protectorate was established, supervising Tan, Heng, Yong, Chen, Lian, Nanliang, Nanyun, and Nanying — eight prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Tan protectorate over eight prefectures.

sentences.zh: 潭州領長沙、衡山、醴陵、湘鄉、益陽、新康六縣。

translations.literal: Tan Prefecture governed Changsha, Hengshan, Liling, Xiangxiang, Yiyang, and Xinkang — six counties.

sentences.zh: 七年，廢雲州，改南梁為邵州，南營為道州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Yun Prefecture was abolished; Nanliang was changed to Shao Prefecture and Nanying to Dao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 7: Yun abolished; Nanliang to Shao; Nanying to Dao.

translations.literal: Xinkang County was abolished.

sentences.zh: 督潭、衡、郴、連、永、邵、道等七州。

translations.literal: It supervised Tan, Heng, Chen, Lian, Yong, Shao, Dao, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Supervised Tan, Heng, Chen, Lian, Yong, Shao, Dao, and others.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Changsha commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣五，戶九千三十一，口四萬四百四十九。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed five counties, with 9,031 households and 40,449 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣六，戶三萬二千二百七十二，口十九萬二千六百五十七。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed six counties, with 32,272 households and 192,657 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師南二千四百四十五里，至東都二千一百八十五里。

translations.literal: It lay 2,445 li south of the capital and 2,185 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 2,445 li south of the capital, 2,185 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Under the Qin the Changsha commandery was established.
Under the Han it was the Changsha kingdom, administered from Linxiang County.
Later Han made it the Changsha commandery.
Wu left it unchanged.

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝置湘州，至梁初不改。

translations.literal: Jin Emperor Huai established Xiang Prefecture; through the early Liang it was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Huai: Xiang Prefecture; early Liang unchanged.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，為潭州，以昭潭為名。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen it became Tan Prefecture, named for Lake Zhaotan.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Tan, from Lake Zhaotan.

sentences.zh: 煬帝改為長沙郡，仍改臨湘為長沙縣。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang changed it to the Changsha commandery and also changed Linxiang to Changsha County.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Changsha commandery; Linxiang to Changsha County.

translations.literal: In the Wude era it was restored as Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 湘潭後漢湘南縣地，屬長沙郡。

translations.literal: Xiangtan, Later Han Xiangnan County territory, subordinate to Changsha commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangtan: Later Han Xiangnan, Changsha commandery.

sentences.zh: 吳分汀南立衡陽縣，屬衡陽郡。

translations.literal: Wu split Tingnan to establish Hengyang County, subordinate to Hengyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Tingnan for Hengyang, Hengyang commandery.

translations.literal: The Sui abolished the commandery and the county was subordinate to Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sui abolished commandery; county to Tan.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude the seat was moved to Luokou and it was therefore changed to Xiangtan County.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: seat to Luokou; Xiangtan County.

translations.literal: Xiangxiang, Han Zhongwu County, subordinate to Lingling commandery.

sentences.zh: 後漢改為重安，，又名湘鄉，屬長沙郡。

translations.literal: Later Han changed it to Chong'an and also called it Xiangxiang, subordinate to Changsha commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Chong'an, also Xiangxiang, Changsha commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢縣，屬長沙國，故城在今縣東八十里。

translations.literal: Yiyang, a Han dynasty county subordinate to the Changsha kingdom; the old city lies eighty li east of the present county.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang: Han county, Changsha kingdom; old city 80 li east.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude Xinkang County was split off.
In the seventh year it was abolished and merged in.

sentences.zh: 漢臨湘縣，界有醴陵，後漢立為縣，屬長沙郡。

translations.literal: Liling, within Linxiang County bounds there was Liling; Later Han established it as a county, subordinate to Changsha commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liling: within Linxiang; Later Han county, Changsha commandery.

translations.literal: The Sui abolished it; in the fourth year of Wude it was split off from Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Sui abolished; Wude 4 split from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 吳分長沙置瀏陽縣，隋廢。

translations.literal: Wu split Changsha to establish Liuyang County; the Sui abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Changsha for Liuyang; Sui abolished.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude it was re-established at the old city.
Heng Prefecture, middle grade, in Sui times the Hengshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Prefecture, middle grade: Sui Hengshan commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平蕭銑，置衡州，領臨蒸、湘潭、耒陽、新甯、重安、新城六縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Heng Prefecture was established, governing Linzheng, Xiangtan, Leiyang, Xinning, Chong'an, and Xincheng — six counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Heng with six counties.

translations.literal: In the seventh year Chong'an and Xincheng — two counties — were abolished.
In the ninth year of Zhenguan You County of the abolished Nanyun Prefecture was assigned here.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 9: You from abolished Nanyun here.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Hengyang commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣五，戶七千三百三十，口三萬四千四百八十一。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed five counties, with 7,330 households and 34,481 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣六，戶三萬三千六百八十八，口十九萬九千二百二十八。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed six counties, with 33,688 households and 199,228 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南三千四百三里，至東都二千七百六十里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,403 li southeast of the capital and 2,760 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,403 li southeast of the capital, 2,760 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Linzheng, Han Zhengyang County, subordinate to the Changsha kingdom.

sentences.zh: 吳分蒸陽立臨蒸縣，吳末分長沙東界郡立湘東郡。

translations.literal: Wu split Zhengyang to establish Linzheng County; at the end of Wu the eastern border of Changsha was split to establish the Xiangdong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Zhengyang for Linzheng; late Wu eastern Changsha for Xiangdong commandery.

translations.literal: Song, Qi, and Liang left it unchanged.

sentences.zh: 隋罷湘東郡為衡州，改臨蒸為衡陽縣。

translations.literal: The Sui abolished the Xiangdong commandery to make Heng Prefecture and changed Linzheng to Hengyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Xiangdong to Heng Prefecture; Linzheng to Hengyang.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude it was again made Linzheng.
In the first year of Kaiyuan it was again made Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 吳分耒陽立新寧縣，屬湘東郡。

translations.literal: Wu split Leiyang to establish Xinning County, subordinate to the Xiangdong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Leiyang for Xinning, Xiangdong commandery.

translations.literal: Formerly administered at Sandong; in the fourth year of Wude the seat was moved to Mazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Former seat Sandong; Wude 4 moved to Mazhou.

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan it was administered at Yijiang.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to Changning.

sentences.zh: 漢縣，屬長沙國，縣北有攸溪故也

translations.literal: You, a Han dynasty county subordinate to the Changsha kingdom; north of the county is the old You Creek.
translations.idiomatic: You: Han county, Changsha kingdom; old You Creek north.

translations.literal: Chaling, a Han dynasty county subordinate to the Changsha kingdom.
The Sui abolished it.
In the fourth year of Wude it was split off from You County.
Leiyang, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Guiyang commandery.
The Sui changed it to Leiyin.
In the fourth year of Wude it was again made Leiyang.
Wu split Xiangnan County to establish it.
Formerly subordinate to Tan Prefecture; later detached to Heng Prefecture.
Li Prefecture, lower grade, in Sui times the Liyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Prefecture, lower grade: Sui Liyang commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平蕭銑，置澧州，領孱陵、安鄉、澧陽、石門、慈利、崇義六縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Li Prefecture was established, governing Canling, Anxiang, Liyang, Shimen, Cili, and Chongyi — six counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Li with six counties.

translations.literal: In the eighth year Canling County was abolished.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Liyang commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Li Prefecture.
At the beginning of Tianbao it was detached to Eastern Shannan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣五，戶三千四百七十四，口二萬五千八百二十六。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed five counties, with 3,474 households and 25,826 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣四，戶一萬九千六百二十，口九萬三千三百四十九。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed four counties, with 19,620 households and 93,349 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南一千八百九十三里，至東都一千五百七十二里。

translations.literal: It lay 1,893 li southeast of the capital and 1,572 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 1,893 li southeast of the capital, 1,572 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Liyang, Han Lingyang County, subordinate to Wuling commandery.

sentences.zh: 吳分武陵西界置天門郡。

translations.literal: Wu split the western border of Wuling to establish the Tianmen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split western Wuling for Tianmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉末，以義陽流人集此，僑置南義陽郡。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin displaced people from Yiyang gathered here and the Southern Yiyang commandery was established as a refugee seat.
translations.idiomatic: Late Jin Yiyang migrants; refugee Southern Yiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，改南義陽為澧州。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen it changed Southern Yiyang to Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Southern Yiyang to Li Prefecture.

translations.literal: All were administered from this county.
Anxiang, the territory of Han Canling County, subordinate to Wuling commandery.
The Sui separately established Anxiang County.
In the eighth year of Wude Canling was abolished and merged in.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Canling abolished and merged in.

sentences.zh: 吳分零陽縣於此置天門郡。

translations.literal: Wu split Lingyang County here to establish the Tianmen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Lingyang here for Tianmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，廢天門郡，以廢州為石門縣

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen it abolished the Tianmen commandery and made the abolished prefecture Shimen County.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Tianmen abolished; abolished prefecture to Shimen County.

sentences.zh: 本漢零陽縣，隋改零陽為慈利縣。

translations.literal: Originally Han Lingyang County; the Sui changed Lingyang to Cili County.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Han Lingyang; Sui Lingyang to Cili.

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wude Chongyi was abolished and merged in.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 8: Chongyi abolished and merged in.

translations.literal: Lang Prefecture, lower grade, in Sui times the Wuling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Prefecture, lower grade: Sui Wuling commandery.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Lang Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Lang established.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Wuling commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，割屬山南東道，舊領縣二，戶二千一百四十九，口一萬九百一十三。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao it was detached to Eastern Shannan Circuit; formerly it governed two counties, with 2,149 households and 10,913 mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianbao: Eastern Shannan; formerly two counties, 2,149 households, 10,913 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶九千三百六，口四萬三千七百十六。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao there were 9,306 households and 43,716 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南二千一百五十九里，至東都一千八百五十八里。

translations.literal: It lay 2,159 li southeast of the capital and 1,858 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 2,159 li southeast of the capital, 1,858 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Wuling, the territory of Han Linyuan County, subordinate to Wuling commandery.
Under the Qin it was territory of the Qianzhong commandery.

sentences.zh: 梁分武陵郡于縣置武州。

translations.literal: The Liang split Wuling commandery and established Wu Prefecture at the county.
translations.idiomatic: Liang split Wuling; Wu Prefecture at the county.

translations.literal: Chen changed Wu Prefecture to the Yuanling commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，復為嵩州，尋又改為朗州。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen it was restored as Song Prefecture and soon again changed to Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Song Prefecture; soon Lang again.

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yang it was the Wuling commandery.
In the Wude era it was restored as Lang Prefecture.
All were administered from Wuling County.
A Sui dynasty county, taking the name of the prefecture.
