Yong Prefecture, middle grade, in Sui times the Lingling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Prefecture, middle grade: Sui Lingling commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平蕭銑，置永州，領零陵、湘源、祁陽、灌陽四縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Yong Prefecture was established, governing Lingling, Xiangyuan, Qiyang, and Guanyang — four counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Yong with four counties.

translations.literal: In the seventh year Guanyang was abolished.
In the first year of Zhenguan Qiyang County was abolished; in the fourth year it was re-established.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Lingling commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣三，戶六千三百四十八，口二萬七千五百八十三。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed three counties, with 6,348 households and 27,583 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶二萬七千四百九十四，口十七萬六千一百六十八。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao there were 27,494 households and 176,168 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師南三千二百七十四里，至東都三千六百六十五里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,274 li south of the capital and 3,665 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,274 li south of capital, 3,665 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Lingling, the territory of Han Quanling County, subordinate to Lingling commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢郡治泉陵縣，故城在今州北二里。

translations.literal: The Han commandery seat was Quanling County; the old city lies two li north of the present prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han seat Quanling; old city 2 li north of present prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，改泉陵為零陵縣，仍移於今理。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen, Quanling was changed to Lingling County and the seat was moved to the present site.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Quanling to Lingling; seat moved.

sentences.zh: 梁、陳皆為零陵郡，隋置永州，煬帝復為零陵郡，皆治此縣

translations.literal: Under Liang and Chen it was the Lingling commandery; the Sui established Yong Prefecture and Emperor Yang again made the Lingling commandery; all administered this county.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Chen Lingling commandery; Sui Yong; Yang Lingling; all at this county.

sentences.zh: 吳分泉陵縣，於今縣東北九十里置祁陽縣，今有古城。

translations.literal: Wu split Quanling County and established Qiyang County ninety li northeast of the present county; the old city still exists.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Quanling for Qiyang 90 li northeast; old city remains.

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen it was merged into Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: merged into Lingling.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan it was again split off and established and moved to the present seat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 4: split again; moved to present seat.

translations.literal: Abolished; in the fourth year established again.

sentences.zh: 石燕岡在祁陽西北一百一十里，此岡穴出石燕，充貢。

translations.literal: Shiyan Ridge lies one hundred ten li northwest of Qiyang; this ridge cave produces stone swallows sent as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan Ridge 110 li northwest of Qiyang; stone swallows from cave as tribute.

translations.literal: The Xiang River comes from the Lingling border to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang River from Lingling border south.

sentences.zh: 漢零陵縣地，屬故城在今縣南七十八里。

translations.literal: Xiangyuan, the territory of Han Lingling County; the old city lies seventy-eight li south of the present county.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyuan: Han Lingling; old city 78 li south.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，並零陵入湘源縣

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen, Lingling was merged into Xiangyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Lingling into Xiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 漢零陵縣地，大業末，蕭銑析湘源縣置。

translations.literal: Xiangyuan, the territory of Han Lingling County; at the end of the Daye era Xiao Xian split Xiangyuan County and established it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyuan: Han Lingling; Daye end Xiao Xian split from Xiangyuan.

translations.literal: Abolished.

sentences.zh: ，荊南節度使呂諲奏，復於故城置灌陽縣。

translations.literal: The Jingnan military commissioner Lü Yin memorialized to re-establish Guanyang County at the old city.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan commissioner Lü Yin: Guanyang restored at old city.

translations.literal: The Guan River is west of the city; it is now called Guanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guan River west of city; now Guanyuan.

sentences.zh: 道州中，隋零陵郡之永陽縣。

translations.literal: Dao Prefecture, middle grade, in Sui times Yongyang County of the Lingling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Prefecture, middle grade: Sui Yongyang in Lingling commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平蕭銑，置營州，領營道、江華、永陽、唐興四縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Ying Prefecture was established, governing Yingdao, Jianghua, Yongyang, and Tangxing — four counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Ying with four counties.

translations.literal: In the fifth year it was changed to Southern Ying Prefecture.
In the eighth year of Zhenguan it was changed to Dao Prefecture and Yongyang County was still abolished.
In the seventeenth year it was abolished and merged into Yong Prefecture.
In the first year of Tianbao it was again split off from Yong Prefecture and established.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Jianghua commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Dao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣三，戶六千六百一十三，口三萬一千八百八十。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed three counties, with 6,613 households and 31,880 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣四，戶二萬二千五百五十一，口十三萬九千六十三。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed four counties, with 22,551 households and 139,063 mouths.
At present it governs five counties.
Yingdao, Han Yingpu County, subordinate to Lingling commandery.
Wu established the Yingyang commandery.
Under the Jin it was changed to the Yongyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，改營浦為永陽縣。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen, Yingpu was changed to Yongyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Yingpu to Yongyang.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude Ying Prefecture was established at the county and it was changed to Yingdao County.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Ying at county; Yingdao County.

translations.literal: In the fifth year the character nan was added.
In the eighth year of Zhenguan it was changed to Dao Prefecture.
In the first year of Tianbao Yingdao was changed to Hongdao.

sentences.zh: 漢泠道縣，屬零陵郡，古城在今縣東界南四十里。

translations.literal: Tangxing, Han Lingdao County, subordinate to Lingling commandery; the old city lies forty li south on the eastern border of the present county.
translations.idiomatic: Tangxing: Han Lingdao, Lingling; old city 40 li south on east border.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，廢泠道入營道縣，仍於泠道廢城置營道縣。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen, Lingdao was abolished and merged into Yingdao County; Yingdao County was still established at the abolished Lingdao city.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Lingdao into Yingdao; seat at old Lingdao city.

sentences.zh: ，移營道縣于州郭置，仍于此置唐興縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude Yingdao County was moved below the prefectural walls and Tangxing County was established here.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Yingdao below walls; Tangxing here.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was renamed Wusheng.
In the first year of Qianyuan it was again made Tangxing.
In the first year of Zhenyuan it was changed to Yantang.
The Ling River is sixty li south of the present county.
translations.idiomatic: Ling River 60 li south of county.

translations.literal: Jianghua, Han Fengcheng County, subordinate to Cangwu commandery.
In the fourth year of Wude Jianghua County was established by splitting Fengcheng County of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Jianghua from He Prefecture's Fengcheng.

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan it was reassigned to Yong Prefecture.
In the third year of Tianbao it returned to Dao Prefecture.
In the first year of Qianyuan it was changed to Yunxi County.
In the second month it was again made Jianghua.

sentences.zh: 隋改漢營浦縣為永陽，置道州。

translations.literal: The Sui changed Han Yingpu County to Yongyang and established Dao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sui: Han Yingpu to Yongyang; Dao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後州郭內置營道縣，乃移永陽之名於州西南一百一十里置。

translations.literal: Later Yingdao County was established within the prefectural walls; the name Yongyang was moved one hundred ten li southwest of the prefecture and established.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yingdao in walls; Yongyang name moved 110 li southwest.

translations.literal: Abolished; the territory entered Yingdao.
In the second year of Tianbao it was again split off from Yingdao.
In the first year of Qianyuan it was changed to Yongming County.

sentences.zh: ，湖南觀察使韋貫之奏請析延唐縣，于道州東南二百二十里舂陵侯故城北十五里置縣，因以大曆為名。

translations.literal: The Hunan observation commissioner Wei Guanzhi memorialized to split Yantang County and establish a county fifteen li north of the old Chunling marquis city two hundred twenty li southeast of Dao Prefecture, taking the name from the Dali era.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guanzhi: split Yantang; county 15 li north of Chunling marquis city; named for Dali.

translations.literal: Chen Prefecture, middle grade, in Sui times the Guiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Prefecture, middle grade: Sui Guiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平蕭銑，置郴州，領郴、盧陽、義章、臨武、平陽、晉興六縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Chen Prefecture was established, governing Chen, Luyang, Yizhang, Linwu, Pingyang, and Jinxing — six counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Chen with six counties.

translations.literal: In the seventh year Yizhang and Pingyang — two counties — were abolished.
In the eighth year Jinxing was abolished.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Guiyang commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣五，戶八千六百四十六，口四萬九千三百五十五。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed five counties, with 8,646 households and 49,355 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣八，戶三萬一千三百三。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed eight counties, with 31,303 households.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南三千三百里，至東都三千五十七里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,300 li southeast of the capital and 3,057 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,300 li southeast of capital, 3,057 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 漢縣，屬桂陽郡，漢郡理所也。

translations.literal: Chen, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Guiyang commandery; it was also the seat of the Han commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen: Han county, Guiyang commandery; Han commandery seat.

translations.literal: Later Han moved the commandery seat to Leiyang and soon returned it to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han seat to Leiyang; soon back to Chen.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊封子弟為桂陽王，皆治於此。

translations.literal: Song and Qi enfeoffed younger princes as kings of Guiyang; all were administered here.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Qi Guiyang kings administered here.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，改為郴州，煬帝為桂陽郡，，改郴州，皆以郴為理。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen it was changed to Chen Prefecture; Emperor Yang made the Guiyang commandery; it was again changed to Chen Prefecture; all were administered from Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: Chen Prefecture; Yang Guiyang commandery; Chen seat throughout.

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era Xiao Xian split Chen to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Daye end: Xiao Xian split from Chen.

translations.literal: Abolished; in the eighth year re-established.
In the fourth year of Zhenguan Gaoping County was established on the southern border of Yizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 4: Gaoping on Yizhang south border.

sentences.zh: ，廢高平，仍移義章治高平廢縣。

translations.literal: Gaoping was abolished and Yizhang was still moved to administer the abolished Gaoping county.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping abolished; Yizhang seat at abolished Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 晉分郴縣置汝城、晉寧二縣。

translations.literal: Under the Jin Chen County was split to establish Rucheng and Jinning — two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Jin split Chen for Rucheng and Jinning.

sentences.zh: 陳廢二縣，立盧陽郡，領盧陽縣。

translations.literal: Chen abolished the two counties and established the Luyang commandery, governing Luyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Chen abolished two counties; Luyang commandery with Luyang.

translations.literal: The commandery was abolished and Luyang was subordinate to Chen Prefecture.
In the fourth year of Wude it was changed to Yichang.
Under the Jin Chen was split to establish the Pingyang commandery and county.
translations.idiomatic: Jin split Chen for Pingyang commandery and county.

translations.literal: Chen abolished it; later Xiao Xian again split Chen to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen abolished; later Xiao Xian split Chen again.

translations.literal: Abolished; in the eighth year re-established.
Later Han split Chen to establish Hanning County.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han split Chen for Hanning.

sentences.zh: 吳改為陽安，晉改為晉甯，隋改為晉興。

translations.literal: Wu changed it to Yang'an; the Jin changed it to Jinning; the Sui changed it to Jinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yang'an; Jin Jinning; Sui Jinxing.

translations.literal: Abolished; re-established and renamed Zixing.
Linwu, the territory of Han Bian County, subordinate to Guiyang commandery.
Under the Jin it was abolished; Chen restored it.
The Sui abolished it.

sentences.zh: ，宇文融析郴縣北界四鄉置安陵縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan Yu Wenrong split four districts of the northern border of Chen County to establish Anling County.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 4: Yu Wenrong split four north districts of Chen for Anling.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to Gaoting, taking the name from a mountain east of the county.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 1: Gaoting, from east county mountain.

sentences.zh: 漢縣，屬桂陽郡，縣南臨武溪故也。

translations.literal: Linwu, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Guiyang commandery; south of the county is the Linwu Creek, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: Linwu: Han county, Guiyang; Linwu Creek south gives name.

translations.literal: Nanping, Han Nanping County, subordinate to Guiyang commandery.
The Sui abolished it.
In the fourth year of Zhenguan Nanping County was re-established.
In the first year of Qianyuan it was changed to Lanshan.
Mount Jiuyi lies fifty li west of the county.

sentences.zh: 邵州隋長沙郡之邵陽縣。

translations.literal: Shao Prefecture, in Sui times Shaoyang County of the Changsha commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Prefecture: Sui Shaoyang in Changsha commandery.

sentences.zh: ，平蕭銑，置南梁州，領邵陵、建興、武岡三縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Southern Liang Prefecture was established, governing Shaoling, Jianxing, and Wugang — three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Southern Liang with three counties.

sentences.zh: 七年：省建興入武岡，省邵陵並邵陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Jianxing was merged into Wugang and Shaoling was merged with Shaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 7: Jianxing into Wugang; Shaoling into Shaoyang.

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan it was renamed Shao Prefecture.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Shaoyang commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Shao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣二，戶二千八百五十六，口一萬三千五百八十三。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed two counties, with 2,856 households and 13,583 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶一萬七千七十三，口七萬一千六百四十四。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao there were 17,073 households and 71,644 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師東南三千四百里，至東都二千二百六十八里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,400 li southeast of the capital and 2,268 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,400 li southeast of capital, 2,268 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Shaoyang, Han Zhaoling County, subordinate to the Changsha kingdom.

sentences.zh: 後漢改為昭陽，晉改為邵陽。

translations.literal: Later Han changed it to Zhaoyang; the Jin changed it to Shaoyang.
When the Sui pacified Chen it was restored at the present seat.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: restored at present seat.

sentences.zh: 吳分零陵北部置邵陵郡。

translations.literal: Wu split the northern part of Lingling to establish the Shaoling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split northern Lingling for Shaoling commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，廢郡，以邵陽屬潭州，尋又于邵陽置建州。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen the commandery was abolished and Shaoyang was assigned to Tan Prefecture; soon Jian Prefecture was also established at Shaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pacified Chen: commandery abolished; Shaoyang to Tan; Jian at Shaoyang.

sentences.zh: ，改置南梁州，，改為邵州，皆理邵陽縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude it was changed to Southern Liang Prefecture and in the eighth year of Zhenguan to Shao Prefecture; all were administered from Shaoyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Southern Liang; Zhenguan 8: Shao; all at Shaoyang.

translations.literal: Wugang, Han Duliang County, subordinate to Lingling commandery.
Under the Jin Duliang was split to establish Wugang County.
The Sui abolished it.
In the fourth year of Wude it was again split off from Shaoyang and established.
Lian Prefecture, in Sui times the Xiping commandery.
In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Lian Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Lian established.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Lianshan commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Lian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣三，戶五千五百六十三，口三萬一千九十四。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed three counties, with 5,563 households and 31,094 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶三萬二千二百十，口一十四萬三千五百三十二。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao there were 32,210 households and 143,532 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師南三千六百六十五里，至東都三千四百五里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,665 li south of the capital and 3,405 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,665 li south of capital, 3,405 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 漢縣，屬桂陽郡，今州理是也。

translations.literal: Guiyang, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Guiyang commandery; the present prefectural seat is here.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang: Han county, Guiyang commandery; present seat here.

sentences.zh: 隋，于縣置連州，大業改為熙平郡，，復為連州，皆以桂陽為理所。

translations.literal: Under the Sui Lian Prefecture was established at the county; in the Daye era it was changed to the Xiping commandery and later restored as Lian Prefecture; all were administered from Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Lian at county; Daye Xiping commandery; Lian again; all at Guiyang.

translations.literal: Yangshan, a Han dynasty county subordinate to Guiyang commandery.
Later Han abolished it.
When the Jin pacified Wu, Hengqu County was split off and restored.

sentences.zh: 梁于浛洭縣西置陽山郡，以縣屬之。

translations.literal: The Liang established the Yangshan commandery west of Hengqu County and the county was subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yangshan commandery west of Hengqu; county subordinate.

translations.literal: The Sui abolished the commandery and the county was subordinate to Lian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sui abolished commandery; county to Lian.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude it was moved north of the Heng River; the present county seat is there.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: moved north of Heng River; present seat.

translations.literal: It is also called the Huang River.

sentences.zh: 晉武分桂陽立廣惠縣，隋改為廣澤。

translations.literal: Jin Emperor Wu split Guiyang to establish Guanghui County; the Sui changed it to Guangze.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wu split Guiyang for Guanghui; Sui Guangze.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to Lianshan.

sentences.zh: 黔中道黔州下，都督府，隋黔安郡。

translations.literal: Qian Prefecture of Qianzhong Circuit, lower grade, protectorate, in Sui times the Qian'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Prefecture, lower grade, protectorate, Qianzhong Circuit: Sui Qian'an commandery.

sentences.zh: ，改為黔州，領彭水、都上、石城三縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude it was changed to Qian Prefecture, governing Pengshui, Dushang, and Shicheng — three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Qian with Pengshui, Dushang, Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 二年，又分置盈隆、洪杜、相永、萬資四縣。

translations.literal: In the second year Yinglong, Hongdu, Xiangyong, and Wanzhi — four counties — were also split off.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 2: Yinglong, Hongdu, Xiangyong, Wanzhi split.

sentences.zh: 四年，置都督府，督務、施、業、辰、智、牂、充、應、莊等州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year a protectorate was established supervising Wu, Shi, Ye, Chen, Zhi, Zang, Chong, Ying, Zhuang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: protectorate over Wu, Shi, Ye, Chen, Zhi, Zang, Chong, Ying, Zhuang, others.

sentences.zh: 其年，以相永、萬資二縣置費州，以都上分置夷州。

translations.literal: That same year Xiangyong and Wanzhi — two counties — were used to establish Fei Prefecture and Dushang was split to establish Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Same year: Fei from Xiangyong and Wanzhi; Yi from Dushang.

translations.literal: In the tenth year Gaofu of Si Prefecture was assigned here.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又以高富屬夷州，以智州信寧來屬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Gaofu again went to Yi Prefecture and Xinning of Zhi Prefecture was assigned here.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 11: Gaofu to Yi; Zhi's Xinning here.

sentences.zh: 今督思、辰、施、牢、費、夷、巫、應、播、充、莊、牂、琰、池、矩十五州。

translations.literal: At present it supervises Si, Chen, Shi, Lao, Fei, Yi, Wu, Ying, Bo, Chong, Zhuang, Zang, Yan, Chi, Ju — fifteen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Now supervises fifteen prefectures including Si, Chen, Shi, Lao, Fei, Yi.

translations.literal: That same year the protectorate was abolished.
The Zhuangzhou protectorate-general was established.
Abolished; Bo Prefecture became the protectorate.
Abolished; Qian Prefecture again became the protectorate.

sentences.zh: ，改黔州為黔中郡，依舊都督施、夷、播、思、費、珍、溱、商九州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao Qian Prefecture was changed to the Qianzhong commandery, still a protectorate over Shi, Yi, Bo, Si, Fei, Zhen, Qin, and Shang — nine prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 1: Qianzhong commandery; protectorate over nine prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又領充、明、勞、羲、福、犍、邦、琰、清、莊、峨、蠻、牂、鼓、儒、琳、鸞、令、那、暉、郝、總、敦、侯、晃、柯、樊、稜、添、普寧、功、亮、茂龍、延、訓、卿、雙、整、懸、撫水、矩、思源、逸、殷、南平、勳、薑、襲等五十州。

translations.literal: It also governed Chong, Ming, Lao, Xi, Fu, Jian, Bang, Yan, Qing, Zhuang, E, Man, Zang, Gu, Ru, Lin, Luan, Ling, Na, Hui, Hao, Zong, Dun, Hou, Huang, Ke, Fan, Leng, Tian, Puning, Gong, Liang, Maolong, Yan, Xun, Qing, Shuang, Zheng, Xuan, Fu, Ju, Siyuan, Yi, Yin, Nanping, Xun, Jiang, Xi, and fifty other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Also fifty jimi prefectures including Chong, Ming, Lao, Xi, Fu, Jian, Zhuang, Zang, and others.

translations.literal: All were jimi prefectures administered from mountain valleys.
After the Zhide era the Qianzhong commandery was again the Qianzhou protectorate-general.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide: Qianzhong to Qian protectorate-general.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣五，戶五千九百一十三，口二萬七千四百三十三。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed five counties, with 5,913 households and 27,433 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶縣六，戶四千二百七十，口二萬四千二百四。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao six counties, with 4,270 households and 24,204 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師南三千一百九十三里，至東都三千二百七十一里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,193 li south of the capital and 3,271 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,193 li south of capital, 3,271 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Pengshui, Han Youyang County, subordinate to Wuling commandery.
Wu split Xiyang to establish the Qianyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu split Xiyang for Qianyang commandery.

translations.literal: The Sui established Pengshui County at the commandery.
Zhou established Feng Prefecture and soon made it Qian Prefecture.
In the fourth year of Wude a protectorate was established at the prefecture.
The Sui split Qianyang County to establish Shicheng County.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to Qianjiang.
In the second year of Wude Hongdu County was split off, administered from Hongdu Creek.
In the fourth year of Zhenguan the seat was moved to Gongtuan.
In the second year of Wude Yinglong County was established west of the Ba River from Pengshui.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 2: Yinglong west of Ba River from Pengshui.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to Yingchuan.
In the first year of Qianyuan it was changed to Yangshui.

sentences.zh: 隋置信安縣，取界內山名。

translations.literal: The Sui established Xin'an County, taking the name from a mountain within the bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Xin'an, from mountain in bounds.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to Xinning.
In the third year of Tianbao it was subordinate to Yi Prefecture.
When the prefecture was abolished it was assigned here.
In the second year of Tianbao it was split off from Yinglong County.
Chen Prefecture, lower grade, in Sui times Yuanling County.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Prefecture, lower grade: Sui Yuanling.

sentences.zh: ，平蕭銑，置辰州，領沅陵等五縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Xiao Xian was pacified, Chen Prefecture was established, governing Yuanling and five other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: Xiao Xian pacified; Chen with Yuanling and five others.

sentences.zh: 九年，分大鄉置大鄉五縣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year five counties were split off from Daxiang to establish Daxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 9: five counties from Daxiang for Daxiang.

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan Xupu County was split off from Chenxi.
In the second year of Tianbao Santing County was split off from Daxiang.
In the second year of Tianbao Xi Prefecture was established by splitting Daxiang and Santing — two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 2: Xi from Daxiang and Santing.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan a protectorate was established supervising Wu, Ye, and Jin — three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 4: protectorate over Wu, Ye, Jin.

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan the protectorate was abolished.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Luxi commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Chen Prefecture, taking the creek name.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide: Chen again, from creek name.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣七，戶九千二百八十三，口三萬九千二百二十五。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed seven counties, with 9,283 households and 39,225 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣五，戶四千二百四十一，口二萬八千五百五十四。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed five counties, with 4,241 households and 28,554 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師南微東三千四百五里，至東都三千二百六十里。

translations.literal: It lay 3,405 li south and slightly east of the capital and 3,260 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,405 li south slightly east of capital, 3,260 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 漢辰陽縣，屬武陵郡，本秦黔中郡縣也。

translations.literal: Chenxi, Han Chenyang County, subordinate to Wuling commandery — originally a county of Qin Qianzhong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxi: Han Chenyang, Wuling; originally Qin Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 隋改辰陽為辰溪，仍分置沅陵縣，仍置沅陵郡。

translations.literal: The Sui changed Chenyang to Chenxi and still split off Yuanling County and established the Yuanling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Chenyang to Chenxi; Yuanling split; Yuanling commandery.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude it was changed to Chen Prefecture with Yuanling as the seat.
In the second year of Tianbao it was split off from Yuanling County.
Luyang, the territory of Han Yiling County, subordinate to Wuling commandery.
In the fifth year of Zhenguan it was split off from Chenxi.
In the fifth year of Zhenguan it was established by splitting Yuanling and Chenxi — two counties.
In the second year of Tianbao Longmen County was split off and established; soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 漢辰陽縣地，隋分置辰溪縣。

translations.literal: Xupu, the territory of Han Chenyang County; the Sui split off Chenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: Xupu: Han Chenyang; Sui split Chenxi.

sentences.zh: 錦州下，，分辰州麻陽縣地並開山洞置錦州及四縣。

translations.literal: Jin Prefecture, lower grade: in the second year of Tianbao territory of Mayang County of Chen Prefecture was split off and mountain caves were opened to establish Jin Prefecture and four counties.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 2: from Chen's Mayang; opened caves; Jin and four counties.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao Jin Prefecture was changed to the Luyang commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣五，戶二千八百七十二，口一萬四千三百七十四。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed five counties, with 2,872 households and 14,374 mouths.

sentences.zh: 至京師三千五百里，至東都三千七百里。

translations.literal: It was 3,500 li to the capital and 3,700 li to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3,500 li to capital, 3,700 li to Luoyang.

translations.literal: The four counties above were all established together with the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Four counties above established with prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其常豐本名萬安，，改為常豐

translations.literal: Changfeng was originally named Wan'an; in the first year of Tianbao it was changed to Changfeng.
In the fourth year of Wude it was split off from Daxiang of Chen Prefecture and was subordinate to Xi Prefecture.
In the second year of Tianbao it was reassigned to Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 施州下，隋清江郡之清江縣。

translations.literal: Shi Prefecture, lower grade, in Sui times Qingjiang County of the Qingjiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Prefecture, lower grade: Sui Qingjiang in Qingjiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 義甯二年，置施州，領清江、開夷二縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yining, Shi Prefecture was established, governing Qingjiang and Kaiyi — two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yining 2: Shi with Qingjiang and Kaiyi.

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan Ye Prefecture was abolished and Jianshi County was assigned here.
In the first year of Zhenguan Kaiyi County was abolished and merged into Qingjiang.
In the first year of Tianbao it was changed to the Qinghua commandery.
After the Zhide era it was again made Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣三，戶二千三百一十二，口一萬八百二十五。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed three counties, with 2,312 households and 10,825 mouths.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣二，戶三千七百二，口一萬六千四百四十四。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it governed two counties, with 3,702 households and 16,444 mouths.

sentences.zh: 在京師南二千七百九里，至東都二千八百一十里。

translations.literal: It lay 2,709 li south of the capital and 2,810 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: 2,709 li south of capital, 2,810 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Qingjiang, Han Wu County, subordinate to Nan commandery.
Wu split Wu to establish Shaqu County.
Later Zhou established Shi Prefecture at the county.
The Sui made it Qingjiang County; it was the seat of the prefecture.
Later Zhou split Wu County to establish Jianshi County.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou split Wu for Jianshi.

sentences.zh: 義甯二年，於縣置業州，領建始一縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yining Ye Prefecture was established at the county, governing Jianshi alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yining 2: Ye at county; Jianshi alone.

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan Ye Prefecture was abolished and the county was subordinate to Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 8: Ye abolished; county to Shi.

sentences.zh: 巫州下，，分辰州龍標縣置巫州。

translations.literal: Wu Prefecture, lower grade: in the fourth year of Wude Longbiao County of Chen Prefecture was split off to establish Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其年，置夜郎、朗溪、思征三縣。
